bull_bear.body:
- Preferential issue during Q1 FY27: 13.00 lakh equity shares and 27.78 lakh convertible warrants allotted at ₹181.71 per share, with ₹23.62 crore of equity received in the quarter.
- On 11 July 2026, 5.00 lakh warrants were converted into equity shares (₹6.81 crore), taking the paid-up share count to 2,17,96,770.
- As of 12 August 2026, 22.78 lakh warrants remain outstanding, convertible within 18 months of allotment; full conversion "brings in a further ₹31.04 crore", described as "contracted to follow".
- Stated use of the raise: the preferential equity "supports the deleveraging agenda" and part-funds the Components expansion.
- Capital employed rose 16.3% QoQ to ₹265.55 crore (Machinery division ₹173.89 crore; Defense & Components division ₹91.67 crore, up 33.4% QoQ "as production ramped"). No dividend or buyback is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Established in 1983, the Company "ranks among India's leading machine tool manufacturers, with a strong position in cam and crank borers, fine borers, and finish milling machines"; the closing slide frames it as "Building India's Precision Engineering & Defense Future".
- Scale markers cited: 43+ years of legacy, 545+ cumulative employee strength, 320+ cumulative years of Board/senior-management domain expertise, 6 manufacturing units across Hyderabad and Pune, 7+ countries' export presence, 5,000+ "happy clients" and 100+ diversified offerings.
- Two-division structure — Machine Tools, and Auto Components & Defence. Deck states "defence revenue is reported within the segments above" (Machinery and Defense & Components), i.e. no separate defence segment line.
- Marquee clientele listed for the Machine Tools division includes John Deere, Ashok Leyland, Volvo Eicher, Suzuki, Tata Motors, Mahindra, Honda, Caterpillar, Cummins, Craftsman Automation, Azad Engineering and Escorts; the Defence division lists DRDO, Northern Command, Assam Rifles, NSG, SSB, CISF, BSF and Small Arms Factory, Kanpur.
- Core competence claimed on three legs: an in-house design team backed by dedicated R&D facilities, AS 9100 and ISO 9000 quality certifications, and "state-of-the-art machinery and manufacturing systems".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [OFAC sanctions] Designated on the OFAC SDN List on 30 Oct 2024 under Executive Order 14024 (basis contested from the outset); wind-down licences expired Dec 2024; two OFAC questionnaires answered Jun–Nov 2025; removed from the SDN List on 30 Jun 2026 with all blocked property unblocked; India's Ministry of External Affairs confirmed the delisting on 8 Jul 2026.
- [What delisting restores] USD and EUR banking channels reopen and access to the US financial system is restored; customers, suppliers and trade financiers "no longer carry secondary-sanctions exposure"; European and US end-markets foreclosed during the designation "become addressable again for the Machinery division". Benefits accrue from Q2 FY27 — the entire Q1 was operated under the sanctions regime.
- [Order book] ₹271.00 crore as of 12 August 2026, split General Purpose Machines ₹103.00 cr (38.0%), Defence ₹98.00 cr (36.2%), Special Purpose Machines ₹37.00 cr (13.7%), Forgings ₹30.00 cr (11.1%) and Job works ₹3.00 cr (1.1%); the deck says this exceeds FY26 revenue of ₹209.62 crore by ₹61.38 crore, "over and above the first quarter's billings".
- [Defence order win] ₹58.21 crore order received on 15 July 2026 from the Ministry of Defence (Army) for 7.62 mm medium machine gun modification kits, part of "indigenous small arms manufacturing orders from the Indian Armed Forces and security establishments".
- [Order book drivers] GPM "adds up quarter on quarter as a low lead-time product" and at 38% of the book "converts to revenue within the year"; SPM "remains steady on critical replacements at OEMs"; Auto Components opportunities come off the recently commissioned hot forging lines.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Lokesh Machines as a 43-year-old Indian machine tool manufacturer — strong in cam and crank borers, fine borers and finish milling machines — now rebuilding around a scaled-up Auto Components & Defence division and the reopening of export channels after its removal from the OFAC SDN List on 30 June 2026.
